corrections: Rebuilt long low fuselage, three forward panes, roof and side apertures, sliding doors, T700 nacelles and upturned exhausts, low fixed wheels and folding-style stabilator from Army dimensions and M photos.
Four wide-chord main blades with swept drooping tips, 3-degree mast tilt and starboard tail rotor with 20-degree cant; no weapons or external tanks.
Four-display M cockpit, central standby instruments, paired flight director controls, deep scalloped coaming and two FMS keypads on a broad console; armored seats and crew controls.
Overlay iterations corrected boom height, tail-rotor side and cant, tail station, blade azimuth, coaming closure and windshield interference; widened panel camera to include all four displays.
limitations: Dimensioned Army drawings depict A/L variants. Shared fuselage dimensions are used; blade chord, exhaust, avionics and optional external stores are resolved from M photographs.
Top-view recognition drawing is low resolution and schematic. Its body planform is a coarse cross-check, not a detailed M engineering drawing.
Panel width 1.63m is an estimate. Near-frontal photo supplies relative positions with uncorrected perspective and lens effects; coaming depth and seat installation remain approximate.
Screens and overhead switch banks are simplified original geometry; detailed electrical systems, mission equipment and all placards are not reproduced.
Reference photographs are local analysis only; no source pixels shipped.

controlReview.checks: Imported GLB control-point movement tested at positive and negative commands; all 20 aircraft pass. Cockpit pairs and all ten airplane exterior pairs visually inspected. Roll, pitch, rudder and declared pedal directions corrected; ailerons and full flap deployment corrected.
limitations: Checks cover existing bindings; Cherokee and Caravan pedal geometry is static.
Full control travel and flight response remain approximations unless independently dimensioned in the model reference notes.
This audit verifies movement; it does not upgrade legacy helicopter avionics or remove previously documented geometry limitations.
